top_story_title: PHP2Shell exploited against internet-exposed appliance management interfaces, starting with Palo Alto Networks
top_story_summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed on Wednesday that attackers are exploiting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against publicly accessible management interfaces: "Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet." The two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 (remote code execution via out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (remote code execution via stale internal request state), were fixed in the PHP Foundation's critical release of October 21 and added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-10-26 with a remediation due date of 2026-10-29 - today. Both are unauthenticated RCE.
top_actions: Inventory every appliance whose management interface (HTTPS/API) is reachable from an untrusted network - firewalls, VPN gateways, load balancers, management servers - and remove that exposure immediately; restrict to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.

Check your running version against the vendor's fixed-release table for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (Palo Alto Networks portfolio advisory, Cisco advisory cisco-sa-php-october26) and schedule the upgrade - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as no fixed build is stated in the reporting.
Federal and KEV-bound operators: the CISA due date for both CVEs was 2026-10-29. Record patched / mitigated / accepted risk against each device group today.
After patching, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, device certificates and VPN pre-shared keys - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Export and review appliance configurations for unexpected admin users, scripts, static routes or modified login pages, and hunt for unexpected outbound connections from management interfaces.
executive_summary: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is being actively exploited against internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces; both CVEs are KEV-listed with a 2026-10-29 due date, and Cisco has published its own portfolio advisory.

Cisco patched CVE-2026-76418, an actively exploited unauthenticated flaw in the ASA/FTD Remote Access SSL VPN that reloads the firewall - the second exploited Cisco firewall VPN zero-day since August, and there are no workarounds.

Cisco Talos attributed KeyDrift, malware that harvests SD-WAN traffic encryption keys, to APT exploitation of CVE-2026-20127 on Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers; Cisco's refreshed advisory extends the peering authentication bypass to Validator (vBond) as well as Controller and Manager.
Lumen and Cisco tied SD-WAN zero-day exploitation to Volt Typhoon's 'Silent Train' covert access network, built from rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices.

The Brotli flaw CVE-2026-111497 (KEV, due 2026-11-10) reaches past Node.js into infrastructure components: Cisco and Palo Alto Networks both published portfolio advisories, and Check Point's analysis says the question to answer is whether attacker-controlled Brotli data can reach a vulnerable decoder.
Cisco issued an informational advisory on the emergency distrust of eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs, whose private keys can be brute-forced in seconds.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Confirm the running ASA/FTD version against Cisco's fixed-release table in the advisory and schedule the upgrade inside the change window, HA pair secondary first - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as no fixed build is stated in the reporting.
**Cisco** — Identify which tunnel groups have secondary authentication configured; those are the exposed path described by Cisco.
**Cisco** — Patch the orchestrator and controllers before edge devices, and validate certificate trust across the fabric after the upgrade.
**Cisco** — Include Validator (vBond) in scope - earlier remediation that covered only Controller and Manager leaves it exposed.
**Cisco** — Patch affected controllers immediately if you have not already; confirm the fix date against your change records rather than assuming February remediation covered every instance.
**Cisco** — Hunt for KeyDrift and for the indicators in the Talos report across all controller instances, including non-production and lab fabrics.
**Cisco** — Schedule the upgrade now rather than at the next cycle; with no workaround, deferral is pure exposure. Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Cisco** — Upgrade the HA pair secondary first and confirm config sync before failing over.

headlines.title: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited ASA and FTD VPN Flaw That Can Crash Firewalls
headlines.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can reload Cisco ASA and FTD firewalls through the Remote Access SSL VPN using CVE-2026-76418, already exploited in the wild.

headlines.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
headlines.summary: A broken peering authentication mechanism lets an unauthenticated attacker gain admin privileges and NETCONF access on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator.

headlines.title: Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN
headlines.summary: Talos found a sophisticated APT, UAT-11473, that exploited the KEV-listed Cisco SD-WAN auth bypass CVE-2026-20127 to deploy malware it calls KeyDrift.

headlines.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense Software Remote Access SSL VPN Tunnel Denial of Service Vulnerability
headlines.summary: Cisco's advisory for the ASA/FTD Remote Access SSL VPN denial-of-service flaw confirms there are no workarounds - only the software update.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco published its portfolio advisory for PHP2Shell - two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws now in CISA KEV with a 2026-10-29 due date.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks rates its PHP2Shell portfolio advisory CRITICAL for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both unauthenticated RCE and both KEV-listed.
